themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 233 THIS WEEK—a 344% increase vs. the 8-week average of 52.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 9.49)—suggesting acute pavement failure, potholes, or surface deterioration affecting major thoroughfares in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 233 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 52.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% spike, z-score: 9.49)
Street condition is the #2 complaint category overall in the district (1,489 complaints over 90 days)
Repeated community board budget request for street reconstruction (DOT) suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Map the specific blocks with the highest complaint density to identify hotspots; interview DOT about repair timelines
Canvass residents and local business owners on street safety hazards and accessibility issues caused by poor pavement conditions

themes_detail.label: Tree Canopy Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints skyrocketed to 58 THIS WEEK—a 487% increase vs. the 8-week average of 9.9 complaints (z-score: 7.77)—compounded by spikes in dead/dying trees (14 complaints, +367%) and overgrown branches (15 complaints, +264%), indicating widespread tree failure or storm damage.
evidence: Damaged tree complaints: 58 THIS WEEK vs. 9.9 weekly average (487% spike, z-score: 7.77)
Dead/dying tree complaints: 14 THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average (367% spike, z-score: 4.59)
Overgrown tree/branches complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average (264% spike, z-score: 5.54)
Total of 87 tree-related complaints THIS WEEK alone (vs. ~27 weekly baseline)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent storms or weather events triggered the spike; check NYC Parks maintenance schedule and budget allocation to this district
Interview Parks Department on branch overgrowth blocking sidewalks and creating hazards; document safety risks for pedestrians and drivers

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk & Obstruction Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints nearly doubled this week to 19 (95% increase vs. 9.8 weekly average, z-score: 6.25), while obstruction complaints reached 43 TWO WEEKS AGO (278% increase vs. 11.4 average, z-score: 6.63), suggesting accumulating debris, broken pavement, and blocked pedestrian pathways across the district.
evidence: Sidewalk condition complaints: 19 THIS WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly average (95% spike, z-score: 6.25)
Obstruction complaints: 43 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 11.4 weekly average (278% spike, z-score: 6.63)
Combined with tree/branch spikes, indicates systematic obstruction of public pedestrian space
reporting_angles: Survey commercial corridors and residential blocks to document specific sidewalk hazards; identify if illegal vendors, construction debris, or abandoned objects are responsible
Interview disabled residents and seniors on mobility barriers; connect to community board's longstanding park maintenance and street improvement requests

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Cleanliness Decline
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 31 THIS WEEK—a 164% increase vs. the 8-week average of 11.8 complaints (z-score: 5.16)—signaling potential litter, rodent activity, or improper waste disposal escalating across neighborhoods.
evidence: Unsanitary condition complaints: 31 THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 weekly average (164% spike, z-score: 5.16)
Water system complaints (876 over 90 days) and sewer complaints (341 over 90 days) remain elevated, potentially related to waste management infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Investigate DSNY collection schedules and staffing in the district; determine if service gaps correlate with spike timing
Document specific neighborhoods with worst conditions; interview Sanitation on rodent control and graffiti removal efforts

themes_detail.label: Traffic Flow & Signal Failures
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked 3 WEEKS AGO to 6 complaints—a 336% increase vs. the 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.65)—while traffic signal condition complaints remain elevated at 559 over 90 days, indicating congestion and malfunctioning infrastructure affecting commuter safety.
evidence: Traffic complaints: 6 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 6.65)
Traffic signal condition is #9 complaint category overall (559 complaints over 90 days)
Spike is slightly older than other issues but remains relevant indicator of transit infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Map traffic signal outages and broken intersections; request DOT maintenance records to assess repair responsiveness
Interview regular commuters and delivery drivers on congestion patterns; connect to broader infrastructure upgrade requests in community board budget submissions
